target_customer: Consumers in Belarus, Russia, Ukraine, Kazakhstan and the US who want to give away or get used items nearby; planned enterprise product for companies
problem: People have unwanted items but no easy, hyperlocal way to pass them on; existing buy and sell or donation platforms were not built around giving.
business_model: consumer marketplace with a virtual currency (Karma coins bought in app, about 30 percent of Karma per TechCrunch) plus ads; planned enterprise recycling product
product_category: consumer peer-to-peer marketplace for used goods (giveaway and auction with virtual coins)

founders.name: Sergei Lepchenkov
founders.background_notes: Habr interview (2020-09) says he was a .NET/C# developer and originator of the idea; co-founders had run businesses before. Education not stated.

founders.name: Artem Artemiuk
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2020-03 names him CMO; Habr says he handles scaling.

founders.name: Siarhei Stasilovich
founders.background_notes: Named by TechCrunch; Habr says he handles finance, operations and legal. Not listed on the YC page.

competitors.name: Goodwill
competitors.what: nonprofit thrift stores with an online auction, named by the founders as a competitor

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile marketplace with auction mechanics, photo tagging via a cloud vision API and moderation; standard consumer app engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Local liquidity (Minsk had over 25,000 listings versus about 3,000 in Moscow per the Habr interview) gives some network effect, but the product is easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acquired or copied it in sources found; the app was reported removed from the iOS App Store and not actively promoted by 2022 per third-party trackers.

market_need_then: Founders were inspired by a store in Austria letting customers take one free item; the app reported over 1 million users and about 400,000 completed item transactions by 2020-09.

branding.name_origin: Launched in Russian-language markets as Otdam Darom (roughly 'giving away for free') and renamed GiveAway for the international market; no source explains the choice of the English name.
branding.domain_note: Uses giveaway.mobi, a .mobi domain, rather than giveaway.com; the site could not be fetched from this session.

identity.voice_and_tone: Community, friendly; internal currency called Karma

branding.brand_signature: Karma virtual currency earned by giving

rebrands.why: Renamed for the international market per the Habr interview; date approximate

branding.community_and_virality: Local community feel with user stories and a nearby feed; about 1,000 organic new US users per day in testing per Habr (2020-09).

brand_strength.rationale: The Russian-language brand had real local traction, but the English name GiveAway is generic, collides with the common word for contests and has a .mobi domain.

outcome_analysis: GiveAway grew fast in Belarus and neighbouring markets, reaching over 1 million users in 2020, but the company was unprofitable in September 2020 and monetised only through Karma purchases and ads. Third-party app trackers show the iOS app removed and not actively promoted by 2022, and no later funding beyond YC was confirmed, so the outcome looks like a stall. The generic English name and weak monetisation are plausible but not confirmed causes.
notes: giveaway.mobi could not be fetched (host did not resolve in this session's network); status of the live site is unknown. Directory status is Active but third-party Adapty pages say the iOS app is removed from the App Store and the other page says last updated 2022-05-27; outcome causes are not public, so failure factors are inferred from the Habr interview (not profitable) and name genericness, not stated by the company. Aggregators (VCBacked $480K, FundedIQ $500K, a 2021-09 pre-seed) were not confirmed by a second outlet so are not recorded as rounds. Competitor sources are dated 2020-09 (about six months after the batch) because no earlier source naming rivals was found.
